items.rule: If two corresponding angles of one triangle are equal to two corresponding angles of another triangle, the triangles are similar.
items.formula: \angle A=\angle D,\quad\angle B=\angle E\implies\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF
items.example: \angle A=50^\circ,\quad\angle D=50^\circ,\quad\angle B=70^\circ,\quad\angle E=70^\circ\implies\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF

items.rule: If one pair of corresponding angles is equal and the including sides are proportional, the triangles are similar.
If all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, the triangles are similar.
Congruent triangles have exactly equal corresponding sides and angles. Common criteria are SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and RHS.
items.formula: \text{SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS}\implies\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF

items.rule: The order of letters in a similarity or congruence statement tells you which vertices and sides correspond.
items.formula: \triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\implies AB\leftrightarrow DE,\quad BC\leftrightarrow EF,\quad CA\leftrightarrow FD

items.rule: For similar triangles, the ratio of any corresponding lengths is constant.
items.formula: k=\frac{\text{corresponding side in larger triangle}}{\text{corresponding side in smaller triangle}}

items.rule: The ratio of perimeters of similar triangles equals their linear scale factor.
The ratio of areas of similar triangles is the square of their linear scale factor.

concepts.title: 1. What Makes Triangles Similar
concepts.subtitle: AA, SAS and SSS Similarity Criteria
concepts.summary: Two triangles are similar when they have the same shape, even if their sizes differ. This can be established by AA, SAS, or SSS conditions.

points.text: SAS: One corresponding angle is equal and the two sides including that angle are proportional.
SSS: All three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.
Shape, not size: Similar triangles may have different side lengths but maintain equal corresponding angles and a constant side ratio.

concepts.trap: Do not call triangles similar merely because one pair of sides is proportional. A complete valid similarity criterion is required.

concepts.title: 2. Corresponding Sides are Proportional
concepts.subtitle: Matching Sides and Solving Missing Lengths
concepts.summary: Once the correspondence between similar triangles is known, corresponding sides must be paired in the same order. Their ratios are equal, allowing missing lengths to be found by cross-multiplication.

points.text: Correspondence: In $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$, A↔D, B↔E and C↔F.
Consistency: Keep the same triangle in the numerator and the same corresponding triangle in the denominator throughout.

concepts.trap: Do not pair sides just because they look visually similar. Use vertex correspondence or the stated similarity order.

concepts.title: 3. What Makes Triangles Congruent
concepts.subtitle: Exact Equality of Corresponding Elements
concepts.summary: Congruent triangles have exactly the same shape and size. Their corresponding sides and angles are equal, and several standard criteria can establish congruence.

points.text: SSS: All three corresponding sides are equal.
SAS: Two corresponding sides and the included angle are equal.
ASA / AAS: Two corresponding angles and a corresponding side are equal.
RHS: In right triangles, the hypotenuse and one corresponding side are equal.

concepts.formula: SSS,\quad SAS,\quad ASA,\quad AAS,\quad RHS\implies\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF
concepts.trap: Do not use SSA as a general triangle-congruence criterion. Two sides and a non-included angle do not always determine a unique triangle.

concepts.title: 4. Scale Factor & Ratio of Areas
concepts.subtitle: From Lengths to Perimeters and Areas
concepts.summary: For similar triangles, every corresponding linear dimension scales by the same factor k. Perimeters scale by k, while areas scale by k².

points.text: Linear Scale Factor: $k=\frac{\text{corresponding larger side}}{\text{corresponding smaller side}}$.
Perimeter: The perimeter ratio is the same as the side-length ratio.

concepts.trap: Do not use k for an area ratio. Areas scale with the square of the linear factor.

worked_examples.title: Type 1: Identifying a Similarity Criterion
worked_examples.problem: In triangles ABC and DEF, ∠A=∠D and ∠B=∠E. Determine the criterion and write the similarity statement.

steps.reason: Two corresponding angle pairs are given equal.
Two equal corresponding angles are sufficient to establish triangle similarity.

steps.calculation: A\leftrightarrow D,\quad B\leftrightarrow E,\quad C\leftrightarrow F
steps.reason: The third vertices correspond automatically once the first two matches are fixed.
The order of letters records the corresponding vertices.

worked_examples.conclusion: The triangles are similar by AA, with correspondence A↔D, B↔E and C↔F.

worked_examples.title: Type 2: Solving a Missing Corresponding Side
worked_examples.problem: Triangles ABC and DEF are similar with A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. If AB=6 cm, DE=9 cm and BC=8 cm, find EF.

steps.reason: The stated vertex order determines which sides correspond.
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional.
Divide by 6 to isolate the unknown side.

worked_examples.conclusion: The corresponding side EF is 12 cm.
